parsed.explanation: The combined regime is set mainly by federal layers that reach every traveller: passport sex-marker restrictions now in effect (Supreme Court, Nov 2025), entry refusal for marker discrepancies with a possible lifetime fraud finding, passport confiscation and stranding, and documented abuse in federal immigration custody (forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse). Federal corrections policy from 2026 and the stopped reporting of trans prisoner numbers add custody exposure. The sub-unit's protective layer is real: a care-access sanctuary, identity-based prison housing documented to 2021 only, and a 2015 surgery-funding provision. It does not pre-empt federal entry, custody or facilities rules. Its 198 incidents are a raw count with no denominator, so they carry little weight. Trespass arrests for restroom use are documented in other sub-units, and this sub-unit's facility rules are not documented either way. Net: a protective sub-unit inside a hostile, enforced national regime.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport sex-marker restrictions in effect; discrepancies trigger refusal and requests for more evidence; possible permanent fraud ineligibility; passports confiscated or blocked, leaving some travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Documented challenge in national courts; existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; no documented sub-unit override at entry.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal entry screening applies regardless of the sub-unit's sanctuary and equality statutes; a document problem at the border can escalate into detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented federal immigration custody abuse of trans men: forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse. Arrest and 24-hour hold for restroom use occurred in another sub-unit.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for this sub-unit's custody or police practice.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy or fraud allegation can lead from entry to federal detention, where documented abuse follows the traveller.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars gender-identity-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities. Four sub-units criminalise some restroom use; this sub-unit is not documented as one of them.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Sub-unit facilities status not documented in the dossier; no trespass offence for this sub-unit is recorded.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rules and any sub-unit rule act together; the dossier does not establish this sub-unit's facility position either way.

care_services.exposure: Federal rules on care for minors, proposed insurance exclusion, subpoenas of hospital records, and 2026 federal corrections policy denying hormones to trans inmates.
care_services.protection: Sub-unit sanctuary law shields families seeking gender-affirming care, including out-of-state families travelling for it, from child-abuse investigation and prosecution.
care_services.interaction: The sub-unit shield does not bind federal subpoenas, federal prosecutors or federal custody; a traveller held federally may lose care regardless of local law.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal rhetoric and a counterterrorism category that lists 'radically pro-transgender' groups alongside violent extremists; a reward scheme aimed at leadership; federal orders to prosecute teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Statement that counterterrorism powers will not target people who merely disagree; several orders blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing reaches visitors through enforcement and custody, while the sub-unit's posture only partly offsets it.

minors_guardians.exposure: For a minor: federal school-directed prosecution threats, passport and marker problems, and records subpoenas. For a guardian: risk of investigation and custody issues if the child is detained or treated federally.
minors_guardians.protection: Sub-unit shield covers families seeking care for a young person, including out-of-state families.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian's care-seeking can be shielded locally but still reached by federal subpoenas or federal custody of the minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 198 raw incidents in 2025 (no denominator), with a documented rise in hate-crime reports in the largest city; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity, but only 23 sub-units have state statutes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Sub-unit nondiscrimination and hate-crime coverage is not individually detailed; a July 2026 analysis places the sub-unit in a top-tier protective-law band.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local protective law may aid recourse, but the dossier shows recorded hostility persisting and no denominator for per-capita risk.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal orders and policies remain in litigation; the prison housing policy is last documented in 2021; sub-unit facility rules unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Court challenges pending; sub-unit identity-based housing and surgery funding are documented but dated; legal-aid FAQ exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Current federal rules determine a traveller's exposure at any given time; sub-unit protections cannot be confirmed as operating in 2026.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both involve entry-based exclusion and a refusal process with weak appeals. This case is similar in border exposure but adds documented federal custody abuse, including sexual abuse and forced labour, which is more severe than exclusion. It is also less uniformly hostile, since the sub-unit has protective machinery. Net: similar tier, slightly higher on the custody axis.

Both have birth-sex or identity-document custody exposure and documented assaults in detention. This case has a more protective sub-unit and no documented cross-dressing arrest statute in this sub-unit, but a broader federal exposure through entry, marker refusals and federal custody policy. Net: similar, slightly higher given the sub-unit's shield.

Both involve entry-port secondary screening and documented detention pathways. This case is lower because it adds documented federal custody sexual abuse and forced labour, and lifetime fraud ineligibility, which exceed the administrative refusal in 0.55-B. It is higher because the sub-unit offers a strong protective layer that 0.55-B lacks.

Both involve a durable national registry and document exposure that follows the traveller. This case has a stronger documented custody abuse record and a more hostile federal posture, but a local protective layer that 0.45-D lacks. Net: similar or slightly lower.

parsed.synthesis: The federal layer governs the traveller's operative exposure: marker-based refusal at entry, possible lifetime ineligibility, passport confiscation, documented abuse in immigration custody, and federal hostility through enforcement and policy. The sub-unit's sanctuary, identity-based housing (dated to 2021) and surgery funding are real protections, but they do not pre-empt federal entry, custody or subpoena power. Sub-unit facility rules, current housing practice and enforcement records are unresolved. The 198-incident count lacks a denominator and carries little weight. On balance the traveller faces a continuous, enforced national exposure partly offset by a protective sub-unit, placing this in the High-to-Elevated band near 0.37.
